hotspot.ref: GRAVITY Collaboration 2018, A&A 618, L10: NIR flares from a hot spot orbiting at ~6-10 R_g, period 45 +- 15 min, clockwise and close to face-on (GRAVITY 2020, 2023); the node angle here is illustrative

flow.ref: radio S ~ nu^0.3 (Falcke et al. 1998); 2.4 Jy at 230 GHz (EHT 2022); NIR quiescence ~1 mJy at 2.2 um (Do et al. 2019, GRAVITY 2020); quiescent X-rays 2e33 erg/s from the hot outer flow (Baganoff et al. 2003)

nir_red.ref: Witzel et al. 2018, ApJ 863, 15: NIR power spectrum ~ f^-2 with a break near 243 min

(LIGO Scientific & Virgo) 2016, PRL 116, 061102: 36 + 29 Msun at 410 Mpc (z 0.09), final 62 Msun spinning at 0.67; the signal swept from 35 to 250 Hz in 0.2 s, peak strain 1.0e-21.
